title: Row, Ḍombī
voice: A caller's line and the crew's answer: Ḍombīpāda watches the Mātaṅgī girl at the crossing and urges the rower on, on the beat of the oar.

lines.en: Between the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā a boat goes by;
the Mātaṅgī girl, plunged in, ferries over in play.
Row, Ḍombī, row, Ḍombī, the way is clear:
by the true guru's feet I'll go again to the Jina's town.
Five oars dip at the prow; the stern rope’s made fast;
bail with the sky-scoop: at the seams no water gets past.
Moon and sun, two wheels; the pulinda, making and unmaking;
two roads, left and right: heed neither, row to your liking.
No cowrie she takes, no coin she takes: she ferries across at will.
Who climbed on a chariot can't row: they sink, shore after shore.

couplets.kept: The two rivers, the boat and the girl plunged in, in the source's order; 'playing' keeps the ease of her crossing.
couplets.letGo: The source does not rhyme here, and neither does this.

couplets.kept: The call struck twice, Row, Ḍombī, as the source strikes bāhatu and ḍombī: absolute rhyme, sung back after every couplet.
couplets.letGo: The off rhyme of uchārā and jiṇaurā.

couplets.kept: Perfect rhyme on fast / past for the source's perfect bāndhī / sāndhi; 'made fast' is the boatman's word for tied.
Off rhyme on unmaking / liking, as the source goes off-rhyme on pulindā / chandā; the riddle of the pulinda left unsolved.
couplets.letGo: 'Creation and destruction' becomes 'making and unmaking', plainer to sing.

couplets.kept: 'No cowrie she takes, no coin she takes' keeps the source's doubled na lei; the chariot-riders sink shore after shore.
couplets.letGo: The source does not rhyme here; neither does this.
